recipe.label: Embroidery

traits.medium: thread-embroidered-looking cloud landscape on woven fabric
traits.texture: visible woven ground and raised thread-like marks with coherent stitch directions
traits.composition: thread directions follow cloud volume and preserve the broad silhouette and blue sky
traits.lighting: soft raking light gives delicate shadows to thread-like ridges

review_checks: light and shadow cloud masses stay distinct
limitations: No machine embroidery file, thread specification or repeatable stitch geometry is generated.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Embroidery example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A towering white cumulus cloud with bright sunlit upper-right lobes and cool shadowed lower-left volumes, rising into a large deep-blue sky. Tiny dark foliage and roofline details sit only along the bottom edge.
Style/medium: thread-embroidered-looking cloud landscape on woven fabric
Color palette: #EAE4D4, #396895, #90ACBA, #F3ECD7, #6F7F91
Materials/textures: visible woven ground and raised thread-like marks with coherent stitch directions
Composition/framing: thread directions follow cloud volume and preserve the broad silhouette and blue sky; Keep portrait orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: soft raking light gives delicate shadows to thread-like ridges
Requested output target: 1024x1536, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original upward sky viewpoint, large lobed cloud shape, light/shadow arrangement and broad upper sky. Foreground remains a small lower-edge suggestion. Do not add a sea, island bay, garden, sunset or rainbow.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
